title: Slotmap Hill Climb
goal: Bring the Mojo port of the Rust slotmap crate to performance parity with Rust, measured on GitHub Actions macOS runners (Apple M2 Pro, virtual). Every round: study, change, test locally, push, run the thorough CI benchmark, compare against the previous round.
harness: Rust: slotmap 1.1.1 with Criterion. Mojo: this port with std.benchmark. Both time one pass over n elements (1K, 100K, 1M) for insert, shuffled get, shuffled remove, iteration over a half-empty map, and re-insertion into freed slots. Mojo/Rust below 1.0 means Mojo is faster. Shared runners are noisy: treat anything under about 15% as noise.

rounds.name: Baseline
rounds.summary: The port as first written. Core SlotMap operations were already within 20% of Rust; the outliers were SecondaryMap insert (2-5x), sparse-map insert/get/remove (1.4-3x), dense and secondary iteration (2-5x), DenseSlotMap remove (1.7x) and HopSlotMap remove at 1M (1.4x).

rounds.name: Layout and growth
rounds.summary: Interleaved slot metadata with values, amortized growth for SecondaryMap, a single swap-remove for DenseSlotMap, a straight-line fast path in the iterators, and SparseSecondaryMap rewritten as a Swiss table with a register-only hasher. Measured with the original Mojo harness (keep() per element), so Mojo insert/remove still carry that overhead. This runner was 2-4x slower than the baseline's in absolute terms on both sides, so compare ratios, not nanoseconds, and read single-case swings such as DenseSlotMap remove at 1M as noise until confirmed.

rounds.name: Honest harness
rounds.summary: Same library code as round 2. Both benchmarks now fold per-element results into a sum instead of a barrier per element, after finding that Mojo's keep() has a memory clobber that spilled the map's state every iteration. Rounds 2, 3 and 4 ran at the same time on GitHub's runners and both languages measured about 2x slower than in the baseline run; several cases swing both ways between rounds 2 and 3 with identical library code (DenseSlotMap insert 0.69x to 1.54x), so this round's per-case numbers are contaminated. The workflow now queues benchmark runs, and round 5 re-measures this code alone with Rust and Mojo interleaved per map.

rounds.name: Hop free list
rounds.summary: HopSlotMap keeps a vacant block's other end in the slot itself instead of a side array, so a removal touches fewer cache lines. Pending CI.

rounds.name: Clean re-measure
rounds.summary: The round-4 code measured alone, with the interleaved runner. Establishes the trustworthy numbers to climb from.

techniques.name: Interleave slot metadata with the value
techniques.target: SlotMap, SecondaryMap, HopSlotMap: get, insert, remove
techniques.detail: Rust stores (version, union{value, next_free}) per slot, so a lookup touches one cache line. The port kept a List of metadata and a separate value buffer: two lines per random lookup. Now one _RawSlot[V] struct holds both. The struct is never handled as a whole value (its value field is uninitialized while vacant), only through pointers, which is what makes it work for any V, including linear (non-Deinitable) values.

techniques.name: Amortized doubling in SecondaryMap
techniques.detail: Inserting a key whose slot index was past the end grew the storage to exactly that index, one slot at a time through a push loop. Shuffled keys produce a new record index about ln(n) times, each a full reallocation. Growth now doubles and the vacant slots are written in one loop. Local: 16 -> 5 ns per insert at 1K.

techniques.name: Single swap-remove in DenseSlotMap
techniques.detail: Removal did two swap_elements plus two pops (eight element moves). It now pops the last element, moves it into the hole and fixes the moved element's slot, like Rust's Vec::swap_remove. Same-machine micro-benchmark after: 5.0 vs Rust 5.2 ns at 100K.

techniques.name: Straight-line fast path in iterators
techniques.detail: A Mojo for loop calls __next__ per element and the compiler does not merge the iterator's vacant-skipping loop with the consumer's loop, so every element paid for re-entering a loop. __next__ now checks the next slot first and only calls a separate skip function when it is vacant. 0.72 -> 0.55 ns per element locally (Rust 0.33-0.41).

techniques.name: Swiss table for SparseSecondaryMap
techniques.detail: First attempt: a Dict[UInt32, position] plus dense key/value lists (fast iteration, slow everything else; the stdlib Dict's find alone cost 4.7 ns). Second attempt: open addressing with linear probing and backward-shift deletion (get 6.8 ns at 100K, branchy iteration). Final: control bytes probed 16 at a time with SIMD, 7/8 load factor, tombstones, iteration by group bitmask, the same design as Rust's hashbrown. Local at 100K: get 3.5 ns (Rust 3.1), insert 16 (Rust 15.8), remove including a copy 3.1 (Rust 12.8 without one).

techniques.name: Register-only default hasher
techniques.detail: The stdlib AHasher's 128-bit folded multiply is written with a bitcast that the compiler lowers through NEON registers (fmov/eor.16b round trips), twice per hash. In a throughput micro-benchmark it costs 1.2 ns; on the critical path of a probe its latency showed up as 5 ns per lookup at 1K. IdxHasher is a multiplicative hash on 64-bit integer registers: 5 -> 2 ns per lookup.

techniques.name: One pass over the slot in SlotMap.insert
techniques.detail: insert() went through _next_key() and _commit(), reading the slot's metadata twice. The common insert now reads and writes the slot once; insert_with_key keeps the two-phase path because it needs the key before the value exists.

techniques.name: memcpy growth and copy for trivial values
techniques.detail: Growing slot storage moved occupied values one at a time with a branch per slot. When V is trivially movable (IsTriviallyMovable) the whole buffer is memcpy'd, uninitialized bytes included; copies use IsTriviallyCopyable the same way. Destruction already skipped the per-slot loop for IsTriviallyDeinitable values.

techniques.name: Stop calling keep() per element
techniques.detail: std.benchmark's keep() is an inline asm with a ~{memory} clobber. Called once per inserted key it forced the compiler to reload the map's fields every iteration: fresh insert measured 4.4 ns with it and 1.3 ns without. Both benchmarks now sum the returned keys/values and black-box the sum once per pass, so both languages consume results the same way.

techniques.name: Criterion BatchSize::PerIteration
techniques.detail: With BatchSize::LargeInput, Criterion clones several full 1M-element maps before timing, and they evict each other from cache; Mojo's iter_preproc runs setup right before each timed pass. That explained the baseline's SlotMap reinsert at 1M reading 54 ns for Rust against 9.6 for Mojo. PerIteration gives both sides the same cache state.

techniques.name: HopSlotMap other_end inside the slot
techniques.detail: The free-list entry {next, prev, other_end} lived in a side array, so removing touched the slot's line plus several lines of that array. other_end now sits in the vacant slot's own next_free field (which SlotMap uses for its free list), and the iterator hops without the side array. Local 1M remove: 13.6 -> 11.4 ns (Rust 10.8).

techniques.name: Iterator loop over local copies of fields
techniques.detail: Copying the iterator's cursor and bounds into locals so the compiler keeps them in registers changed nothing: it already did. Kept out.

techniques.name: Pointer cursor instead of an index
techniques.detail: Replacing the index with a slot pointer to save the index-scale instruction per element measured identically (0.55-0.58 ns). Reverted for simplicity.

techniques.name: Linear probing with backward-shift deletion
techniques.detail: Simpler than a Swiss table and fine at 1K, but at 100K get cost 6.8 ns and iteration 6.5 ns per element: with random occupancy, a branch per entry mispredicts constantly. Replaced by control-byte groups.

techniques.name: Dict index plus dense lists
techniques.detail: The original design. Iteration was 8x faster than Rust (it walked dense lists) but insert/get/remove were 1.4-3x slower: every lookup went through the stdlib Dict and then two more arrays, and a removal needed a second hash lookup to fix the moved element's index.

techniques.name: Compile with -O3 for auto-vectorization
techniques.detail: Rust vectorizes the benchmark's sum over dense values; Mojo compiles even a plain pointer loop summing Ints to scalar code, at every optimization level (checked in the emitted assembly; explicit SIMD loads do vectorize). This is a compiler property, not something the library can change.

techniques.name: libc realloc for growth
techniques.detail: Mojo's allocator goes through its own aligned_alloc, so handing its pointers to libc realloc is not known to be safe. A direct measurement showed allocation cost is the same as libc malloc in both languages, so growth is not where the small-size gap comes from.

techniques.name: Interleave Rust and Mojo per map
techniques.detail: The runner used to run all Rust benchmarks (about 10 minutes) and then all Mojo ones, so any drift in the runner's speed became a Rust-vs-Mojo difference. Now each map's Rust and Mojo benchmarks run back to back.

issues.title: The fuzz test never exercised get_disjoint_mut
issues.detail: A planted bug in the pointer arithmetic of get_disjoint_mut passed 300 fuzz seeds. Instrumenting the fuzz showed zero successful disjoint calls: clear and drain were 2 of 9 operations, so the map was emptied every ~5 operations and four valid keys were never alive at once. The op mix now makes those rare and picks recent keys; the same mutant now fails.

issues.title: Parallel shell calls share the working directory
issues.detail: Two tool calls run at once share one shell state, so a cd in one made the other's relative paths miss, silently running stale binaries. Every command now uses absolute paths.

issues.title: A stale precompiled package shadowed the source
issues.detail: A leftover slotmap.mojoc next to probe files made imports resolve to an old build, which looked like a compiler bug for a while.

issues.title: Int(UInt32.MAX) folds to -1
issues.detail: A Mojo constant-folding bug (modular/modular#7154, being fixed upstream). The port uses a literal constant instead.

issues.title: keep() is not black_box
issues.detail: Mojo's keep() clobbers memory; Rust's black_box does not. Using it per element made the Mojo insert benchmark three times slower than the library actually is.

issues.title: Criterion batching changed the cache state
issues.detail: BatchSize::LargeInput cloned several 16 MB maps ahead of timing; the 5.6x 'Mojo win' on reinsert at 1M in the baseline was this artifact.

issues.title: Null key collides with the empty marker
issues.detail: The first hash table used UInt32.MAX as its empty marker, which is also the null key's index, so `null_key in map` could read a stale version and answer yes. Caught by an existing test.

issues.title: Timer resolution at 1K elements
issues.detail: perf_counter_ns reports microsecond steps on this Mac, so 1K-element local numbers are quantized to 1 ns per element. Local numbers guide direction only; CI numbers decide.

findings.title: Codegen is at parity for the core paths
findings.detail: Disassembling both: Rust's SlotMap get loop is 13 instructions, Mojo's 14; iteration 9 vs 10. Same-machine micro-benchmarks put Mojo at or ahead of Rust for SlotMap insert, get and remove. The remaining CI differences come from harness details and from a few structural items listed below.

findings.title: No auto-vectorization of reductions
findings.detail: The one gap the library cannot close: summing over a DenseSlotMap's contiguous values is a vectorized loop in Rust and a scalar loop in Mojo.

findings.title: Hash latency vs throughput
findings.detail: A hasher that benchmarks at 1.2 ns in a throughput loop can still cost 5 ns per lookup when its result feeds the next memory access. Measure hashers on the dependent path.

findings.title: Random occupancy defeats per-entry branches
findings.detail: Any loop that branches on whether each entry is occupied mispredicts about half the time on a random table. Group bitmasks (16 control bytes, one branch per group) fix both iteration and probing.

learnings.group: Where the time actually went (the port's own mistakes)

items.title: Two cache lines per lookup
items.detail: Slot metadata lived in one array and values in another, so every random lookup touched two lines; Rust's slot is one struct. Interleaving them closed most of the get and insert gaps.

items.title: Exact-size growth
items.detail: SecondaryMap grew to exactly the incoming key's index, one slot at a time. That was the 2-5x insert slowdown, fixed by doubling in one function.

items.title: The wrong hash-table shape
items.detail: The sparse map went Dict-plus-lists (fast iteration, slow everything else), then linear probing (branchy), then a Swiss table like hashbrown. Only the last hit parity on all four operations.

items.title: Small structural costs add up
items.detail: Two swaps plus two pops instead of one swap-remove, reading a slot twice on insert, and a side array for Hop's free list each cost 20-70% on one operation.

learnings.group: Compiler and stdlib (what the library cannot change)

items.title: No auto-vectorization of reductions
items.detail: Rust vectorizes a sum over a dense array; Mojo emits scalar code for Int, UInt64, Int32 and Float64 at every -O level, with no loop metadata disabling it. This is the remaining gap on DenseSlotMap iteration.

items.title: Iterator loops do not fuse
items.detail: A for loop calls __next__ per element and the compiler will not merge the iterator's skip loop with the consumer's loop. A straight-line fast path in __next__ recovered about 25%.

items.title: Hasher latency is not throughput
items.detail: AHasher costs 1.2 ns in a pipelined loop but about 5 ns when its result gates the next memory access: its 128-bit multiply is lowered through NEON registers. A register-only hasher cut sparse lookups from 5 to 2 ns.

items.title: Random occupancy defeats per-entry branches
items.detail: An 'is this slot occupied?' branch mispredicts about half the time on a random table. Group bitmasks over 16 control bytes fix probing and iteration alike.

items.title: Codegen is otherwise on par
items.detail: Rust's get loop is 13 instructions, Mojo's 14; iteration 9 vs 10. Same-machine micro-benchmarks put SlotMap insert, get and remove at parity or ahead.

items.title: keep() is not black_box
items.detail: Mojo's keep() clobbers memory, so per-element calls forced the map's state to reload every iteration and tripled the measured insert cost. Both benchmarks now sum results and black-box the sum once per pass.

items.title: Criterion batching changed the cache state
items.detail: Cloning several 16 MB maps ahead of timing made the baseline's 'Mojo 5.6x faster at reinsert' an artifact. PerIteration batching matches Mojo's setup-then-time pattern.

items.title: Local 1K numbers are quantized
items.detail: The timer steps in microseconds, so local runs at 1K elements resolve to 1 ns per element. Local runs pick directions; CI decides.

items.title: CI runners differ 2-4x in absolute speed
items.detail: Round 2's VM measured memory-bound operations 2-4x slower than round 1's, for Rust and Mojo alike. Only the Mojo/Rust ratio within one run is comparable across rounds, and a single-run swing on one case still needs a second run before it counts.

items.title: Never run benchmark jobs concurrently
items.detail: Three CI benchmark runs dispatched together each measured both languages about 2x slower than a lone run, and identical code swung 0.7x to 1.5x between two of them. The runners share hosts. The workflow now serializes benchmark runs, and Rust and Mojo alternate per map inside a run so drift lands on both sides of each ratio.

items.title: The fuzzer never reached get_disjoint_mut
items.detail: clear and drain were 2 of 9 operations, so four valid keys were never alive at once and a planted bug survived 300 seeds. Instrument a fuzzer's per-operation coverage before trusting it.

items.title: Parallel shell calls share a working directory
items.detail: A cd in one call made another's relative paths miss and run stale binaries. Absolute paths everywhere.

items.title: Stale build outputs shadow source
items.detail: A leftover .mojoc next to probe files made imports resolve to an old build and looked like a compiler bug.

items.title: Int(UInt32.MAX) folds to -1
items.detail: A Mojo constant-folding bug, already reported upstream (#7154).
